sentences.text: Pandoravenator was a theropod dinosaur ranging from small to medium size, measuring several meters in total length.
Its skeleton featured a long and slender tail, indicated by the stretching of the tail bones.
Elongated projections on the tail vertebrae suggest that this appendage was stiffened for balance.
The foot bones show a condition similar to arctometatarsalian forms, where the third metatarsal is squeezed between the second and fourth, though the upper surface remains uncompressed.
In the rear tail vertebrae, the back joints are elongated to overlap the back half of the bone body.
Paleontologists Oliver Rauhut and Diego Pol discovered and described this animal in 2017.
The fossils were unearthed in the Cañadón Calcáreo Formation within Chubut Province, central Patagonia, Argentina.
This specific site sits twelve kilometers north of the Cerro Cóndor trail on the western bank of the Chubut River and was nicknamed Pandora's Box because of the many bones found there.
Diego Pol found a unique ankle and foot joint that differed significantly from other finds, which led to the naming of a new species.
The genus name Pandoravenator combines a reference to Pandora's Box with the Latin word for hunter, venator.
The species name fernandezorum honors the Fernández family, who supported the research for twenty years.
The holotype specimen dates to approximately 157 million years ago, during the Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages.
Although the fossils were thought to belong to a single individual, only most of the hind limb parts were designated as the holotype with subnumbers MPEF PV 1773-3 to 18, 27, 28.
According to Rauhut, the ankle construction of Pandoravenator represents an intermediate morphology between the most primitive Ceratosauria and the most derived Tetanurae.
Rauhut and Pol suggest that the unique developmental pattern of the bird-like astragalus arose at the base of Averostra when ceratosaur and tetanuran lineages diverged in the late Early Jurassic.
Pandoravenator was described by Rauhut and Pol in 2017.
Pandoravenator is classified as a theropod dinosaur within the family Tetanurae.
Pandoravenator is placed very basally within the Tetanurae.
